RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Wednesday,  the December 10, 2008/Agrahayana 19, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Commerce and Industry; Defence; Earth Sciences; Home Affairs;
Labour and Employment; Rural Development; Science and Technology;
Textiles)
Total number of questions — 20
42
Problems faced by handloom weavers
*121. SHRIMATI VIPLOVE
THAKUR:
SHRI N.K. SINGH:
Will the Minister of TEXTILES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has conducted
any survey recently to find out the
problems being faced by the weavers;
(b) if so, the details in this regard;
(c) whether Government has made any
effort to improve their lot by improving
handloom clusters, ensuring adequate
supplies of yarn to weavers and extending
health insurance cover for them; and
(d) if so, the details in this regard?
Status of implementation of Assam
Accord
*122. SHRI BIRENDRA PRASAD
BAISHYA: Will the Minister of HOME
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Union Government had
fulfilled all its obligations as committed
through the Assam Accord, 1985;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) if so, the status about each of the
obligation fulfilled till June, 2008 and to be
fulfilled, with specific time limit;
(c) whether all safeguards are provided
in terms of clause 6 of the Accord;
(d) if so, the details of status on each
safeguard promised;
(e) if not, the reasons therefor and the
target set for each;
(f) the specific promise made for the
preparation of National Register of Citizens
(NRC) during tripartite meeting held in
2005 and its status till August, 2008; and
(g) the reasons for delay and target set?
Impact of international economic
meltdown on Indian economy
†*123. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that due to
international economic meltdown several
Indian industries have started decreasing
their production;

43
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) if so, the details of such industries;
(c) whether these industries were
requested to reduce prices of their products
instead of decreasing or stopping
production;
(d) if so, the reaction of the industries
thereto; and
(e) the details of industries wherein
measures have been taken by Government
so far to reduce production cost?
Effect of Rupee instability on import
and export
†*124. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI SHIV ANAND TIWARI:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that due to
instability of Rupee vis-a-vis international
currencies particularly, Dollar, Pound etc.,
the Indian Foreign Trade suffers losses from
time-to-time;
(b) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto; and
(c) the effect of said instability in the
value of Rupee on Indian import and export
in each of the financial years from 2004-05
to 2008-09?
Threat posed by illegal Bangladeshi
immigrants
*125. SHRI V . HANUMANTHA
RAO:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether with a Parliamentary Panel
expressing concern over the threat posed
by illegal Bangladeshi immigrants to nation's
internal security, Government is going to
be under pressure for identifying and
deporting them;
(b) whether the large presence of illegal
Bangladeshi immigrants poses a grave threat
to the internal security;
(c) whether recently the Rajasthan
Government has also conveyed to the
Union Government its concern over the
illegal Bangladeshi immigrants; and
(d) if so, the steps Government
proposes to take to see that all illegal
Bangladeshis are deported back to their
country?
Decline in index of Industrial
production
*126. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
SHRIMA TI SUPRIYA SULE:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether a negative growth of 3.3
per cent in intermediate goods in September
compared with 10 per cent in the
corresponding period last year pulled down
growth in the index of industrial production
to 4.8 per cent in September, 2008 as
against 7 per cent in the same month last
year;
(b) if so, what were the main reasons
and what are the steps being considered in
this regard;
(c) whether the industry has urged
Union Government to focus on small and
medium entrepreneurs to push up the
industrial production; and
(d) if so, what are the other concrete
measures Government proposes to take in
this regard?
